hints: Apply Newton's second law to each particle: $7g - T = 7a$ for $P$ and $T - 3g = 3a$ for $Q$.
Add the equations to find the common acceleration $a$: $(7 - 3)g = (7 + 3)a$.
Use $v^2 = u^2 + 2as$ with $u = 0$ and $s = 0.4\text{ m}$ to find the speed of $P$ immediately before hitting the ground.
walkthrough:
Write the equations of motion for particles $P$ and $Q$:
$$7g - T = 7a$$
$$T - 3g = 3a$$

Add the equations to eliminate tension $T$ and solve for acceleration $a$:
$$(7 - 3)g = (7 + 3)a \implies 4(10) = 10a \implies a = 4\text{ m s}^{-2}$$

Calculate the speed of $P$ immediately before impact using $v^2 = u^2 + 2as$:
$$v^2 = 0 + 2(4)(0.4) = 3.2 \implies v = \sqrt{3.2} \approx 1.79\text{ m s}^{-1}$$

State the results:
$$\text{Acceleration } = 4\text{ m s}^{-2}\text{ with } P\text{ downwards}, \quad \text{Speed } = 1.79\text{ m s}^{-1}$$

ai_rubric.Solving Connected-Particle Systems: Uses $7g-T=7a$ and $T-3g=3a$, obtaining Acceleration $=4\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$ with P downwards; speed $=1.79\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$.

teacher_walkthrough: Particles $P$ of mass $7\text{ kg}$ and $Q$ of mass $3\text{ kg}$ are connected by a light inextensible string over a smooth pulley.

Write Newton's second law for the descending particle $P$:
$$m_P g - T = m_P a$$
$$7(10) - T = 7a \implies 70 - T = 7a$$

Write Newton's second law for the ascending particle $Q$:
$$T - m_Q g = m_Q a$$
$$T - 3(10) = 3a \implies T - 30 = 3a$$

Add the two equations to eliminate $T$:
$$(70 - T) + (T - 30) = 7a + 3a$$
$$40 = 10a \implies a = \frac{40}{10} = 4\text{ m s}^{-2}$$

The particles start from rest ($u = 0$) and $P$ falls through distance $s = 0.4\text{ m}$. Use $v^2 = u^2 + 2as$:
$$v^2 = 0^2 + 2(4)(0.4) = 3.2$$
$$v = \sqrt{3.2} \approx 1.7889\text{ m s}^{-1} \approx 1.79\text{ m s}^{-1}$$

hints: When $P$ hits the ground, $Q$ has risen $0.4\text{ m}$, so its remaining distance to the pulley is $0.5 - 0.4 = 0.1\text{ m}$.
After $P$ hits the ground, the string goes slack and $Q$ moves freely under gravity ($a = -g = -10\text{ m s}^{-2}$) with initial speed squared $v^2 = 3.2$.
Calculate the height $h$ that $Q$ would rise to come to rest using $0 = v^2 - 2gh$, and compare $h$ with $0.1\text{ m}$.
walkthrough:
Find the distance from particle $Q$ to the pulley at the instant $P$ hits the ground:
$$d_{\text{remaining}} = 0.5 - 0.4 = 0.1\text{ m}$$

Calculate the additional height $h$ particle $Q$ would ascend under gravity ($a = -10\text{ m s}^{-2}$) before coming to instantaneous rest:
$$0 = v^2 - 2gh \implies 0 = 3.2 - 2(10)h \implies 20h = 3.2 \implies h = \frac{3.2}{20} = 0.16\text{ m}$$

Compare $h$ to the available distance:
$$\text{Since } 0.16\text{ m} > 0.1\text{ m}, \quad Q\text{ reaches the pulley before coming to rest. Answer: No}$$

ai_rubric.Solving Connected-Particle Systems: Uses the shared tension and common acceleration in compatible equations for the connected particles, obtaining No; Q does not come to rest before reaching the pulley.

teacher_walkthrough:
When $P$ hits the ground, $Q$ has ascended by $0.4\text{ m}$. Its new distance below the pulley is:
$$d = 0.5 - 0.4 = 0.1\text{ m}$$
Once $P$ hits the ground, the string becomes slack ($T = 0$), and $Q$ moves upward freely under gravity with initial upward speed squared $v^2 = 3.2$ and acceleration $a = -g = -10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

Calculate the distance $h$ required for $Q$ to decelerate to instantaneous rest ($v_{\text{final}} = 0$):
$$v_{\text{final}}^2 = v^2 + 2as$$
$$0 = 3.2 + 2(-10)h$$
$$0 = 3.2 - 20h$$
$$20h = 3.2 \implies h = \frac{3.2}{20} = 0.16\text{ m}$$
Since $Q$ needs $0.16\text{ m}$ to come to rest, but the pulley is only $0.1\text{ m}$ above it, $Q$ hits the pulley before stopping.

Conclusion:
$$\text{No; } Q \text{ does not come to instantaneous rest before reaching the pulley}$$
